candidates.rationale: Donated: A's TS_DELTA($close,3) (3 nodes, freed from A's own DIV/epsilon-guard) and B's $book_per_share*$leverage (3 nodes, freed from B's own earnings-yield ratio). A is a pure short-term price-reversal signal with zero capital-structure information; B is a static leveraged-book quality ratio with zero price-dynamics information. Ranking each independently (sidestepping both parents' own wrappers and their different natural scales) and multiplying conditions the 3-day reversal on how much leveraged book capital sits behind the name -- a reversal-weighted-by-financial-leverage-exposure signal neither parent alone expresses.

Donated: A's $book_per_share*$leverage (3 nodes) and B's $high-$low (3 nodes), each independently cross-sectionally ranked to avoid both parents' own wrappers (A's earnings-yield denominator, B's TS_RANK(...,63)/CS_RANK(TS_STD(...)) pair) and to avoid one raw scale swamping the other. A alone is a static balance-sheet ratio with no volatility content; B alone is a pure price-dispersion/volume-vol signal with no capital-structure content. The product highlights highly levered, book-heavy firms that are ALSO trading through an unusually wide daily range today -- leverage amplifies the economic stakes of a volatility episode, an interaction neither factor sees alone.

Donated: A's TS_STD($volume,21) (3 nodes) and B's TS_STD($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes). Each is standardized with CS_ZSCORE rather than A's/B's own CS_RANK wrapper (which would restate their exact 4-node branch) and rather than raw multiplication (volume's far larger raw scale would otherwise swamp the fundamental term). A alone reads trading-tape instability with no fundamental content; B alone reads book-value instability with no market-microstructure content. The interaction flags names where BOTH the tape and the balance sheet are simultaneously unstable -- a compounded-uncertainty signal distinct from either single-domain volatility read.

Donated: A's TS_STD($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes) and B's TS_DELTA($close,3) (3 nodes), combined as a ratio rather than either parent's own rank-spread structure. Dividing the price move by fundamental instability treats a stable balance sheet as a clean-signal amplifier and an unstable one as noise to discount: the same 3-day reversal reads as more informative when the firm's book value has been steady, and gets discounted when the fundamentals themselves are erratic (where a price swing is more likely a rational reaction to real uncertainty than mispricing). Neither parent alone conditions its signal on the other's information.

Same donated pair as pair 4 (A's TS_DELTA($close,3), B's TS_STD($book_per_share,63)) but fused in the opposite spirit on purpose: instead of dividing the price move by fundamental instability (treating instability as noise to discount), this multiplies them (treating instability as amplifying evidence). A 3-day reversal in a name whose book value is ALSO gyrating reads as a deeper mispricing/distress signal, not a cleaner one. Same two ingredients, opposite economic hypothesis -- both are genuine interactions neither parent expresses alone, matching this archive's own precedent of fusing one parent pair two legitimate, opposite ways.

Donated: A's TS_STD($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes) and B's TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes); A's other leg, $accrual_gap, is folded in as a bare field (not the 2-node CS_RANK($accrual_gap) A itself uses) to complete the earnings-quality story A only half-supplies elsewhere in this batch. A alone flags accrual/book-value risk with no trading-activity confirmation; B alone flags a raw volume shift with no fundamental-quality context. The three-way product surfaces names where accrual-flagged earnings quality, balance-sheet instability, AND a fresh shift in trading interest all point the same direction at once -- a compounded quality-meets-attention signal no single parent expresses.

Donated: A's TS_MEAN($roa,63) (3 nodes, the ROA half of A's ROE-minus-ROA spread, freed from A's own SUB/ZSCORE-of-the-whole-spread) and B's TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes). Each is standardized via CS_ZSCORE to avoid both parents' own wrappers and their scale mismatch. A alone is a static profitability level with no trading-activity content; B alone is a raw volume shift with no fundamental-quality context. The product reweights 'is trading interest picking up' by 'is this a fundamentally profitable business': a volume surge in a high-ROA name reads as informed accumulation, the same surge in a weak-ROA name reads as noise -- a conditioning neither parent expresses alone.

Donated: A's TS_DELTA($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes, wrapped in SIGN rather than A's own RANK so only its direction survives) and B's TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes). SIGN() deliberately discards the book-value-change magnitude and uses only its direction as a switch on the volume-change magnitude: the same volume shift reads as a positive signal when book value per share is expanding (buyback/accretion) and a negative one when it is shrinking (dilution/erosion). This also sidesteps the scale mismatch a raw product of a share-count delta and a dollar-per-share delta would otherwise create. A alone has no trading-activity content, B alone has no capital-structure content.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.

  B [cade0742cc483e45]  CS_RANK($earnings_per_share / ($book_per_share * $leverage + 1e-8))

  B [7fb55b403fa3ca08]  TS_RANK($high - $low, 63) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($volume, 21))

pair 3
  A [7fb55b403fa3ca08]  TS_RANK($high - $low, 63) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($volume, 21))
  B [69e04c35904ee838]  CS_RANK($accrual_gap) - CS_RANK(TS_STD($book_per_share, 63))

pair 4
  A [69e04c35904ee838]  CS_RANK($accrual_gap) - CS_RANK(TS_STD($book_per_share, 63))
  B [cf8910d8f4106571]  RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_DELTA($close, 3) / ($close + 1e-8))

  A [cf8910d8f4106571]  RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_DELTA($close, 3) / ($close + 1e-8))
  B [69e04c35904ee838]  CS_RANK($accrual_gap) - CS_RANK(TS_STD($book_per_share, 63))
